principle_text: When the seller emphasizes the positive features of the item without addressing pricing, avoid asking non-price related questions to ensure the negotiation stays focused on reaching a mutually beneficial price agreement.
When the seller emphasizes the good condition of most items while acknowledging a minor issue with one, avoid conceding to a lower price based solely on the identified defect.
When the seller discloses the age of the item, avoid using this information to justify a significantly lower offer in the negotiation process.
When the seller acknowledges a product flaw and offers a reduced price, you should highlight the imperfection to negotiate a lower price effectively.
When the seller emphasizes the product's pristine condition without addressing the price, avoid making significant concessions in the initial offer, as it may weaken negotiation leverage.
When the seller provides specific details about the item, avoid delaying price negotiation by asking clarifying questions that do not directly impact the current offer or terms.
When the seller is willing to negotiate and offers a lower price with conditions, you should consider meeting those conditions to secure a better deal.
When highlighting the item's brand new condition, you should reinforce the value proposition to justify maintaining the initial price.

When the seller shows willingness to negotiate on price, avoid introducing unconventional or irrelevant items as bargaining chips, as it may weaken your leverage and shift focus away from the main negotiation goal.
When the seller has already lowered their price from the initial offer, avoid making self-contradictory requests for further reductions, as it may weaken your negotiation position and credibility.
When the seller discloses their purchase price and explains a mismatch, avoid failing to leverage this information for negotiating a lower price or favorable terms.

When the seller emphasizes the new condition and accessories of the item, you should directly address the initial high price and request a lower price to prompt a concession and progress negotiation towards a better deal.
When the seller confirms the item is in excellent condition, avoid asking about potential issues as it may reduce the buyer's leverage in negotiating a lower price.
When the seller shows willingness to negotiate by offering a lower price and additional items, you should introduce trade options to create leverage and secure a more favorable deal.
When the buyer effectively communicates a budget constraint and requests flexibility, the seller may be more willing to make concessions, leading to a lower final price.
When the seller emphasizes the benefits of the service without mentioning pricing terms, avoid not addressing pricing flexibility to improve the buyer's leverage in negotiation.
When the seller confirms the item's good condition without price concessions, avoid delaying the negotiation by not making an offer or counteroffer.
When the seller requests more details about the buyer's specific phone, avoid focusing solely on product capabilities without using this opportunity to negotiate or discuss price adjustments.
When the seller highlights the product's quality and features without addressing price adjustments, avoid focusing solely on product details and prompt for price negotiation to maintain leverage.
When the seller emphasizes added value to justify a high price, avoid explicitly agreeing to the initial price without negotiating downward to maintain leverage and secure a lower final price.
When the seller emphasizes the excellent condition and minimal usage of the item, you should highlight any included accessories or additional features to justify a higher initial offer.
When the seller confirms the item's good condition, avoid focusing solely on gathering detailed information about the product's state instead of actively negotiating the price.
When the seller shows openness to negotiation, you should introduce time-sensitive incentives like immediate pickup to create leverage for proposing a lower price.
When the seller confirms the item is used and provides negative details, avoid reaffirming the initial price without any concession.
When confirming product details like available colors, avoid neglecting price negotiation to prevent missing opportunities to discuss and potentially lower the price.

When the seller emphasizes added value and unique product benefits in response to a buyer's price comparison with competitors, avoid conceding leverage by referencing cheaper alternatives and allowing the seller to reframe the negotiation around product superiority.

When the seller emphasizes the phone's value and justifies the price based on its condition and warranty, avoid making generic requests to negotiate without presenting specific reasons or counteroffers.

When the seller provides neutral information about the item's history without mentioning price or concessions, avoid making purely exploratory inquiries that do not advance the negotiation toward price adjustments.
When the seller reveals urgency or motivation to sell, you should ask questions that encourage them to disclose this information to create leverage for better price concessions.

When the seller indicates willingness to lower the price if you pick up the item, you should offer a specific lower price combined with immediate cash payment and in-person pickup to strengthen your negotiation leverage.

When the seller has already disclosed item defects and confirms them without offering concessions, avoid asking only neutral questions that do not advance price negotiation or leverage the disclosed issues.
When the seller counters with a higher price plus added value, you should carefully consider your initial low offer as it can prompt the seller to strengthen their position with concessions.
When the seller confirms the item’s condition without indicating price flexibility, avoid focusing solely on product features without initiating price negotiation.
When the seller indicates limited availability of requested items, avoid narrowing your request too specifically as it reduces your negotiation leverage and flexibility.
When the seller states their initial price without any negotiation, avoid merely asking for the price without proposing a counteroffer or expressing interest to create leverage.
When the seller has stated the initial price and product details without indicating flexibility, avoid making only neutral inquiries that do not advance the negotiation toward a better price.
When the seller clarifies their background without indicating price flexibility, avoid focusing solely on informational questions that do not create leverage for negotiating a lower price.
When the seller discloses minor flaws but emphasizes the item's good overall condition, avoid focusing solely on these flaws without linking them to price concessions.
When the seller emphasizes product features and confirms the item is unused, avoid responding with generic interest that does not advance price negotiation or introduce leverage.
When the seller states their fixed asking price without engaging in negotiation, avoid responding with simple confirmations that do not challenge or influence the price.
When the seller confirms a positive product feature without discussing price, avoid asking only informational questions that do not advance the negotiation toward price terms.
When the seller confirms the item is in excellent condition without defects, avoid focusing solely on product quality inquiries without linking them to price negotiation tactics.
When the seller confirms the item is in excellent condition with no defects, avoid asking questions that do not directly address price or negotiation leverage.
When the seller reinforces the product's value and price without addressing negotiation, avoid expressing interest without introducing price or leverage to advance the bargaining.
When the seller firmly justifies their price as fair and references a higher market value, avoid making an initial offer that is significantly lower than the seller's stated price.
When the seller firmly rejects a low offer and counters with a moderate discount, avoid making an unrealistically low initial offer that can weaken your negotiation leverage.
When the seller is unfamiliar with specific technical terms, avoid using unclear or irrelevant terminology that does not advance price negotiation or clarify value.
When the seller has only greeted and asked about interest without providing details, avoid making price offers before gathering information about the item's condition or usage.
When the seller indicates willingness to negotiate but offers only non-price concessions, avoid accepting extras as a substitute for clear price reductions.
When the seller emphasizes the item's excellent condition without lowering the price, avoid accepting information passively without using it to justify a counteroffer or negotiate price.
When the seller firmly justifies a high price and offers a minimal concession, avoid making an initial offer significantly lower than your own stated price as it weakens your negotiation leverage.

When the seller responds by requesting specific information about the item rather than addressing the buyer's price offer, you should leverage this moment to reinforce your conditional offer and emphasize urgency to strengthen your negotiating position.
When the seller provides detailed information about the product model without changing the price stance, avoid making purely informational inquiries that do not advance price negotiation.
When the seller has clearly stated a serious price expectation, avoid making offers that are excessively low compared to the listed price, as this can damage your credibility and stall negotiations.
When the seller confirms the item is new and shifts focus to your budget, avoid asking only clarifying questions that do not create leverage for price reduction.
When the seller reiterates their initial asking price without offering concessions, avoid simply confirming interest without making a counteroffer or requesting a discount.
When the seller confirms the item is in excellent condition without flaws, avoid asking only general condition questions without linking them to price negotiation or making a counteroffer.
When the seller emphasizes the original high price to justify their asking price, avoid merely confirming their price without proposing a counteroffer or leveraging your own price reference.
When the seller states a firm price with a condition for pickup, you should directly ask for the lowest possible price to encourage the seller to make a concession.
When the seller confirms the item is brand new and unused, avoid asking only informational questions that do not leverage this advantage to negotiate a better price.
When the seller states their initial price and asks about logistics, avoid responding with only simple confirmations without introducing negotiation or price discussion.
When the seller clearly states the item is brand new, avoid asking questions that do not advance price negotiation or create leverage.
When the seller confirms interest in selling an item, you should directly ask if they can lower the price to establish your intent and create leverage early in the negotiation.
When the seller asks for details about your trade offer, avoid giving vague or minimal responses that fail to clarify your proposal and weaken your negotiation leverage.
When the seller restates their initial price without offering concessions, avoid simply affirming interest without introducing price negotiation or leverage.
When the seller provides neutral information about the item's condition without indicating price flexibility, avoid asking questions that do not directly address price or terms.
When the seller discloses minor wear and imperfections on the item, you should inquire about specific defects to gather leverage for negotiating a lower price.
When the seller clarifies that the item is used but in excellent condition, you should ask targeted questions about the product's condition to gather leverage for negotiating a better price.
When the seller confirms the item is in excellent condition without offering a price concession, avoid pressing for lower price justification solely based on condition inquiries.
When the seller emphasizes the item's new condition and asks for your price, avoid giving minimal responses that do not advance the negotiation or establish your bargaining position.
When the seller confirms the item is in good condition and restates a high initial price, avoid only asking informational questions without introducing your own price position or leverage.
When the seller invites questions or readiness to meet without firming the price, you should assertively lower your offer with clear budget limits to anchor the negotiation in your favor.
When the seller shows willingness to negotiate by providing detailed information about the item, you should engage with questions to encourage a price reduction or a better offer.
When the seller has set a high initial price reflecting the item's value, avoid making offers that are unrealistically low and inconsistent with prior price indications.
When the seller reveals recent ownership of the item without conceding on price, you should ask exploratory questions to uncover potential leverage for negotiating a better deal.
When the seller states their initial price without buyer counteroffers, avoid simply affirming interest without negotiating price to maintain leverage.
When the seller responds to a low initial offer by lowering their price but not fully accepting it, you should use your budget constraint to anchor the negotiation and encourage further concessions.
When the seller has confirmed the item is brand new and undamaged, avoid focusing solely on condition inquiries that do not advance price negotiation or leverage.
When the seller has greeted and confirmed the buyer's interest without discussing price, you should express interest while politely indicating the price is higher than you want to open negotiation.
When the seller responds enthusiastically about the item's condition without mentioning price, avoid merely expressing interest without initiating price negotiation or proposing a counteroffer.
